description:
## Goal

When `Types::instantiate` is given a concrete `Ty`, return that existing handle before cloning its descriptor or asking `Types::intern` to rediscover it. An empty substitution is likewise an exact identity on every `Ty`.

## Evidence

The current implementation clones its input descriptor, recursively asks whether it contains variables, then re-interns the unchanged descriptor when no substitution can apply. The newly landed fz-kdt.48.12 boundary census found 2,373 similar identity shortcuts on `fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz`; instantiation is the next local algebraic identity on the contract-application path.

## Design

Use the existing `Types::unchanged` path from fz-kdt.48.12. Do not add a substitution cache, type hash, raw descriptor comparison, or a second normalization authority. A type that may contain a substituted variable still follows the ordinary recursive instantiation and sole interning boundary.

## TDD / acceptance

First prove concrete nested types and empty substitutions leave the interning-work census unchanged except for one identity shortcut. Prove a matching substitution still produces the existing specialized `Ty`, and a nonmatching substitution preserves semantics. Re-measure the exact enum fixture under the boundary census; document the added shortcut count. Focused type/canon/three-door fixture tests, formatting, workspace check and strict Clippy pass.

comments.text: Measured on the exact `fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz` type-boundary census. On top of fz-kdt.48.12, concrete/empty instantiation shortcuts add 10,021 direct reuses (2,373 -> 12,394); raw index probes fall 140,419 -> 126,171. Normalizations hold at 11,875 and inserts at 1,033, confirming this removes identity churn without hiding genuinely changed descriptors.

title: Retain concrete Ty through instantiation
